summary: CI pipelines failing to create ephemeral GKE namespaces: org-level conditional IAM binding requires MFA and denies service account impersonation
description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral GKE namespace provisioning in the staging CI pipeline is failing when the pipeline tries to impersonate the CI service account. This started after an org-wide IAM change that introduced conditional bindings enforcing MFA for role grants. Human users are unaffected; the failure impacts non-interactive CI jobs that must impersonate a service account to create namespaces and attach IAM roles.

Impact:
- All staging CI runs that create ephemeral GKE namespaces are failing (blocking PR merges that run integration tests).
- Nightly regression pipeline is failing for ~12 teams.
- Workloads cannot exercise staging infra, delaying test coverage for release candidates.

Environment:
- GCP org: redwood-org (org-id masked)
- Projects impacted: staging-infra, staging-services
- Region: us-central1
- CI runner: github-actions hosted runners impersonating serviceAccount:ci-runner@staging-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Steps to reproduce (straightforward failure):
1) From a GH Actions job configured to impersonate the CI SA: `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@staging-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=staging-infra`
2) Command fails with a permission/error.

Observed behavior (sample error):
- `ERROR: (gcloud.auth.print-access-token) PERMISSION_DENIED: Permission iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied on serviceAccount ci-runner@staging-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com (or condition evaluation failed)`
- GCP Audit log entry: `AccessDenied: Binding evaluation failed for principal serviceAccount:ci-runner@staging-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com; condition 'request.auth.claims.multifactor_auth == true' not satisfied`

Expected behavior:
- CI runners should be able to impersonate CI service accounts for ephemeral infra provisioning in staging without being blocked by human-only MFA conditions.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and quick checks:
- 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: First failure observed by nightly CI (alert from SRE).
- Confirmed change: security rolled out org-wide conditional binding on 2026-03-09 that attaches to roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator with condition checking JWT claims (multifactor flag).
- Pulled org IAM policy with: `gcloud organizations get-iam-policy ORG_ID --format=json` and found conditional binding: 
  - role: roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
  - members: group:human-mfa-exempt@redwood.com
  - condition: `expression: request.auth.claims.multifactor_auth == true`
- Service accounts do not present an MFA claim; condition evaluates to false and the binding does not apply to them. As a result, impersonation attempts evaluate to DENY even though the serviceAccount is a member under a different binding.
- Ran `gcloud logging read` to locate the audit log showing `CONDITION_EVAL_FALSE` for the ci-runner principal.
- Verified that human users can still obtain tokens because they meet the MFA claim requirement.

Hypotheses:
1) The org-level conditional IAM policy was intended to enforce MFA for interactive users but was applied at a scope that includes service account impersonation calls.
2) There is no explicit exception for internal CI service accounts or for calls that originate from workload identity / server-to-server flows.

Commands run (for reproducibility):
- `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@staging-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com` -> PERMISSION_DENIED
- `gcloud organizations get-iam-policy ORG_ID --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.condition!=null)'` -> shows the MFA condition binding

Short-term mitigations tried and status:
- Attempted to add a project-level unconditional binding for roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to the CI service account; rejected by policy automation (security guardrails) for being a broad exception.
- Created a scoped temporary binding using `gcloud beta iam roles` but security automation rolled it back when detected.
comments: Arjun Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-10 10:05 UTC]: Filing ticket — blocking CI for many teams. Noticed this started after the org MFA condition rollout. Need a scoped exception for CI service accounts or alternate approach to allow impersonation from CI runners.

Priya Nair (Assignee) [2026-03-10 12:30 UTC]: Investigating. Can Security confirm intended scope of the MFA conditional binding? If it's intended for human users only we should craft a narrow exception for service accounts used by Github Actions and our CI fleet.

Eve Lawson (Security) [2026-03-11 09:00 UTC]: Security confirms the MFA requirement is intentional for interactive roles. We wanted coverage org-wide but did not anticipate blocking server-to-server impersonation. We need justification and expiry for any exception. Suggested approaches: (a) create an unconditioned role limited to the staging project for impersonation; (b) use Workload Identity Federation with an attribute that can be used in the condition.

Arjun Patel [2026-03-11 11:17 UTC]: Workload Identity Federation option looks promising but will take ~3 days to implement across GH Actions workflows. Requesting a temporary scoped binding for staging with a 72-hour TTL as an emergency workaround.

Priya Nair [2026-03-12 08:45 UTC]: Drafted a minimal ACL change: add member serviceAccount:ci-runner@staging-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com to a project-level binding for roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator with the same condition negated (expression: true) restricted to resource '//cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/projects/staging-infra'. Pushed to infra PR #2817 for review (linked above). Security has not yet approved.

Eve Lawson (Security) [2026-03-12 12:30 UTC]: We will not approve a binding that negates the condition at org scope. Approved option: create a new role `roles/redwood.ciTokenCreator` with minimal permissions and bind it to the CI SA at the project scope with a 72-hour TTL and documented remediation. Please add justification and an automation ticket to remove the exception after rollout of WIF.
next_steps:
1) Add a project-scoped minimal role (roles/redwood.ciTokenCreator) granting only necessary token create permissions, bind to ci-runner@staging-infra with a 72-hour expiry. Security to approve and add to automation to scrub after TTL.
2) Implement Workload Identity Federation for GH Actions to emit an attribute that satisfies the MFA conditional expression or update the condition to accept a service-account attribute. Target ETA: 3 days.
3) Post-mortem to be written once WIF rollout completes; include checklist to avoid applying human-only conditions at org scope without explicit service account exceptions.
4) Update CI runbooks to include steps for emergency temporary exception requests and required justification template.
workaround: Temporary plan approved by Security: create project-scoped role `roles/redwood.ciTokenCreator` (least privilege) and bind to ci-runner@staging-infra for 72 hours. CI to be switched to use that binding immediately; follow-up to migrate GH Actions to Workload Identity Federation.
